## `Verified -1` on patchset 1 root-caused: not a defect in this change

Re-derived from the live run rather than from notes. Run
[35510440501](https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/35510440501) against patchset 1
(rev `f2200580a17`) failed in exactly one matrix cell — `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` —
with exactly one test:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_worker_cancellation_survives_job_completion_race
      - worker 'gw3' crashed while running [...]

    1 failed, 20443 passed, 80 skipped, 29 warnings in 1076.81s

That test is untouched by this change, which streams Jira DC harness test progress. The
crash is the opcert teardown join hanging until xdist kills the worker — bug
`68a9-2a6c-d9aa-49ad`, fixed by change 3009, merged at 14:46:33Z as `641531e62e5`.

## Why a rebase, not a `recheck`

`recheck` would not have helped, and this is worth recording because the instinct is wrong
here. `gerrit-verify.yaml` checks out **the exact patchset** via
`checkout-gerrit-change-action` (`_build-and-test.yml:57`); there is no rebase-onto-target
step. Patchset 1's parent was `e84e4c5e943`, which predates both `e50e733aaa3` and the fix
at `641531e62e5`, so a re-run would have tested the same wedged tree and failed identically.

The fix has to be *in this change's own history* for CI to go green, so patchset 2 is a
clean rebase onto `641531e62e5`. `Change-Id`, `rebar-ticket:` trailer and sign-off all
carried forward; no content change — `git rebase` reported no conflicts and the diff is
unchanged.

This also is not a retry of a flaky test. The flake was root-caused, fixed, reviewed and
merged as its own change; rebasing onto that fix is picking up the remedy, not re-rolling
the dice.
